title: Structured sparse equivariant support × Mirror code
hypothesis: A shared six-coordinate sparse support plus per-material Mirror coefficients recovers aligned conservative material residuals with at least 25% fewer actual bytes than independent sparse adaptation while beating a matched native shared-support control.
physical_object: Shared radial energy basis and shared pretrained-like base potential
mirror_coordinate: Per-material values on a shared six-entry update support

development.selection_metric: select six shared support coordinates by aggregate absolute dev coefficient residual

success_gate: Held-out combined energy/force nRMSE <=0.02, exact force consistency and rotation equivariance, >=25% actual-byte reduction vs independent sparse payload, and a quality/storage or compute advantage over native shared-support coefficient control.
failure_gate: Exact native-control alias, failure of byte/quality gate, or violation of conservative/equivariant physical constraints.
boundaries: Scoped synthetic conservative radial-potential mechanism screen only; not PA300 or MACE-MP reproduction.
Fresh support remains sealed until protocol and dev support selection are committed.
implementation_amendment_01: Before fresh access, payload review found independent_sparse serialized values derived from the dense fit rather than the selected sparse fit. Corrected payload to serialize the exact sparse-fit coefficients used for evaluation; no fresh world was opened.
